text:
elaine (PM): kicking off thread for the "surge governor" rollout plan — this is the feature to gracefully throttle/evict traffic during cross-region capacity pressure. want to capture canary strategy, flag surfaces, customer opt-outs, and rollback ladders.

sam (eng): high level: runtime will expose a policy layer + per-tenant score. important: make flag toggles fine-grained (global, region, tenant). canaries should exercise both normal and degraded paths.

maya (sre): agree. SLA side: we need a clear degradation matrix. e.g. latency SLOs with 3 bands: normal / degraded (cached responses) / eviction (fallback model). customers must see transparent reason codes.

tom (ml): ML note: we must avoid quality cliffs when we switch to smaller model variants. recommend shadowing shorter-context models before active failover, with A/B metric delta < 2% for hallucination/accuracy on our evals.

jordan (cs): from customers: top tenants want explicit opt-out for automatic eviction, and a notification contract (webhook/email) when their requests are demoted. Can we include a per-tenant holdback flag?

sam (eng): yes — design: feature flag hierarchy -> {global, geo, tenant}. flag keys: surge_governor.enabled, surge_governor.level, surge_governor.holdback.tenants[]. We'll include TTLs so ops can auto-clear temporary holds.

elaine (PM): draft rollout phases:
- Phase 0: internal dogfood + assert metrics (2 weeks)
- Phase 1: invite-only low-risk tenants (5%) with notif hook + manual kill-switch
- Phase 2: soft enable for 20% of traffic with auto-rollback triggers
- Phase 3: general availability with tiered defaults
Are those timings realistic?

maya (sre): timings ok but add a preflight: run a shadow run for 48h across 5 regions to capture KV cache hit regressions. also add circuit-breaker: if error rate > 0.5% over 10m, auto-failover to previous routing.

sam (eng): adding canary batch details: batches of 1000 requests per region every 15m, compare lat/err/quality against baseline. automation will promote on stable deltas for 3 consecutive batches.

tom (ml): make sure we log per-sample model variant info to correlate quality regressions. suggestion: include a mini-eval set per tenant for continuous monitoring.

alex (sales): customers will ask about pricing when we demote to cheaper variants. we should expose expected unit-cost delta in the console and in the webhook payload.

jordan (cs): also need a clear contract for enterprise customers: 1) opt-out, 2) emergency override, 3) audit log. legal already requested auditability for on-prem deployments.

elaine (PM): decision proposals:
1) default behavior: auto-govern with conservative thresholds for hosted free tier; enterprise tenants set policy to manual.
2) expose per-tenant holdbacks + webhook for notifications.
3) rollback ladder: soft-disable -> shadow -> full disable -> rollback to previous model.
Please vote thumbs up/down or propose edits.

sam (eng): +1. add a granular flag to disable auto-bump for model variants.

maya (sre): +1. require an ops-approved ticket for manual override that lasts >24h.

tom (ml): +1 but request metric gating: we gate on both latency and quality.

aj (jordan spelled wrong?) jordan (cs): +1 from CS. will draft customer-facing FAQ and notify enterprise AMs.

deploy-bot: deploy check: surge-governor feature branch passes CI (unit/integration). staging deploy window booked Thu 03:00 UTC.

elaine (PM): next steps/action items:
- sam: write feature flag schema + API surface (ETA Wed)
- maya: define SLO/alert thresholds + rollback scripts (ETA Fri)
- tom: set up tenant mini-evals + logging schema (ETA Fri)
- jordan: draft customer FAQ + opt-out flow (ETA Mon)
- alex: pricing blurb for console and webhook (ETA Mon)
- eng ops: plan staging canary run (Thu)

sam (eng): capturing note: flag YAML prototype:
```
surge_governor:
  enabled: true
  mode: auto  # auto | manual | shadow
  level: safe  # safe | aggressive
  tenant_overrides:
    - tenant_id: t-123
      holdback: true
      ttl: 86400
```

maya (sre): logging snippet for rollback trigger: `ROLLBACK_REASON=surge-governor:error_rate>0.5%` — we'll surface this in telemetry + audit log.

elaine (PM): thanks all. will convert into a lightweight playbook and link to shiproom. leave any dissent here; otherwise we'll go with the plan and start Ph0 tomorrow. :rocket:
